incoming.explanation: The neighbour-cluster and settler-stream detail is carried, on the record side, in the Weymouth-community unit.

outgoing.explanation: Extends the associate-network reading: John's land-neighbours, like his 1641 co-petitioners, were established Weymouth men - the reception-into-an-existing-community pattern.
That John's land-neighbours were an established Aylesbury-Vale regional cluster frames his grants as reception into a settled community, reinforcing the admitted-inhabitant reading.

shortLabel: Grants sat inside an Aylesbury-Vale Bucks neighbour cluster (reception)

sources.alignmentNote: The Bucks-cluster extracts and the sworn 1688 deposition establish the Aylesbury-Vale origins of John's Weymouth land-neighbours; the Mass. Archives 129:16 deposition rides on this compiled source.
sources.locator: vol. 3 (Randall of Wendover; Brandon of Ashton Clinton; Hunt/Humphrey of Lee); joint Humphrey-Randall deposition, Massachusetts State Archives 129:16 (2 July 1688)

statement: John Gurney's East and Mill Field neighbours formed a coherent Aylesbury-Vale Buckinghamshire settler cluster - Robert Randall of Wendover, William Brandon of Ashton Clinton, and the Hunt/Humphrey families of Lee, whose Buckinghamshire origins are sworn in a 1688 Weymouth deposition (Massachusetts State Archives 129:16) - so his grants mark him as a newcomer received into an established, regionally-clustered Weymouth neighbourhood. The bearing of this cluster on John's own English origin is developed in the immigration-by-association topic, not here.
